content.text:
I searched the whole document separately for all 19 playbook rules and submitted one plan each. Summary of where the review should focus:

**Likely deviations (redline candidates)**
- **GOVLAW** — Para 27.2 (p0263) deliberately refuses to designate any governing law, and 27.1 (p0262) makes Management Committee referral (possibly foreign arbitration) the sole and exclusive remedy. No accepted law, no court venue.
- **WARRANTY** — Para 4.9 (p0126–p0127) expressly disclaims all representations and warranties on Supplier performance, Wet Segment reliability and system integration.
- **LD** — Para 23.1–23.2 (p0255–p0256) permits capacity reclamation with no payment or credit and forfeiture of amounts already paid, plus default interest (p0153).
- **T4C** — Para 18 (p0228–p0233): 25-year lock-in, no convenience exit during the Initial Period, and no capital-cost credit on withdrawal.
- **INSURANCE** — Para 5.3 (p0139) makes insurance optional only; effectively absent.
- **TRANSITION** — Only Terminal Station continuity and asset liquidation (p0231, p0257, p0234); no data return or migration assistance.

**Compliant / note-only**
- **LOL-CAP** (p0242–p0245 mutual exclusion; no aggregate cap), **INDEMN** (p0241, Paragraph 32 pro-rata mutual regime), **ASSIGN** (22.3 affiliate/successor freedom, p0247–p0250), **AUDIT** (Paragraph 9 mutual; cost-shifting in p0167 noted), **IP** (asset ownership per Schedule B; no IP assigned away), **LICENSE** (IRU is indefeasible; terms deferred per p0209), **RENEWAL** (evergreen, no auto-renewal), **MINCOMMIT** (consortium cost shares; Paragraph 13 uplift mechanics to confirm).

**Absent, no comment needed** — NONCOMPETE, EXCLUSIVITY, MFN, NOSOLICIT (the "exclusive"/"compete" hits are dispute-remedy and "competent jurisdiction" language only).
